Title: How can we help?
Summary: First steps and common tasks.
Body:
Using this help

Choose a category and topic on the left. Search accepts several words, such as copy verification, and searches titles and article text without requiring accents. Back and Forward visit previously opened articles; Home opens the introduction. Ctrl+F focuses search, Alt+Left returns to the previous article and Esc closes help. The selected category expands automatically.

Numbers in screenshots match the explanation below each picture. Click a picture to open its enlargement; the slider changes magnification and scrollbars reveal details. Screenshots show the actual application using generated demonstration data. File names, contents and paths are not taken from user files.

Choose your task

  • Browse and select files, then copy or move them.
  • Open previews, read CSV as a table or convert images.
  • Convert audio with VBR/ABR or work with metadata.
  • Undo an available transaction, resolve a locked file or troubleshoot a problem.

Title: Panels, tabs and selection
Summary: Source and destination panels, layout and selection.
Body:
Current workflow

Open tabs occupy the path row itself. Each panel has its own tabs: + or Ctrl+T opens one, Ctrl+W closes one. Bookmarks under the star are a separate saved list. Short paths stay compact; long paths retain the drive and path ending. Disconnected drives, unavailable FTP locations and deleted folders show an unavailable-location state without losing the saved tab.

Main window orientation

Navigation, selection and columns

Arrow keys change the current item; Enter opens a folder or file. Tab switches the active panel. Click a column heading to change sorting and drag its edge to resize it. Distinguish the current row from the complete selection. Before a batch action, verify the selected-file count in its dialog. Switching to thumbnails does not change folder contents.

Enter another folder or network path in the address field. An access failure does not mean a folder is empty: check existence, permissions and connection availability. Use linked browsing for matching directory structures. See workspaces for favorite locations and saved layouts.

Common folders in the drive selector

The drive selector includes Desktop, Downloads, Documents, Pictures, Music, Videos and the user folder below the drives. Actual Windows known-folder paths are used, including redirection into OneDrive. Selecting one opens that folder directly. While browsing, the closest matching common folder is selected.

Right-click files and folders

A short right-click marks or unmarks only that item. Other marks are preserved and no menu opens. This also works with Windows-style selection enabled. Right-drag marks or unmarks a continuous range and never opens a menu.

Hold the right button on an item without dragging. After 250 ms, feedback labelled File Compass menu appears; at 600 ms the application menu opens. Releasing after it opens does not toggle a mark. Escape cancels the gesture without changing selection. Holding on a member of a marked group preserves the group; holding on an unmarked item targets that item.

The application menu offers Open, F3 Preview, F4 Edit, Shift+F4 External edit, F5 Copy, F6 Move, clipboard, rename, delete and archive commands. Unavailable commands are disabled; less frequent commands are grouped under More commands. The last item is Windows menu, which opens the standard shell context menu and extensions for supported local files. A long press itself no longer opens the native menu. Remote and archive entries use the application menu. The menu key and Shift+F10 open the File Compass menu directly.

Title: Preview, viewer and editor
Summary: F3, F4 and Ctrl+Q.
Body:
Current workflow

Preview and details use unified controls. A selection of supported files can be browsed with a thumbnail strip; the active item is enlarged. Documents and images can be mixed according to preview capabilities. Video can show several still frames extracted locally with FFmpeg; this is not a video player. Editing always targets a specific document rather than the whole selection at once.

Inspect files without an external application

F3 opens the selected file in the viewer; Ctrl+Q toggles quick preview in a panel. F4 opens an editor and can allow changes, so distinguish editing from previewing. Supported formats determine whether the viewer shows an image, document or text. Unsupported or damaged documents may provide only a text excerpt or a limitation message.

Text-preview controls

  • Auto selects a suitable view. Text displays decoded characters; Binary and Hex display bytes for technical inspection.
  • Encoding determines how bytes become characters. For incorrect accents, check UTF-8, BOM or the appropriate legacy code page.
  • Wrap text changes long-line display without modifying the file.
  • Formatted preview switches between a table or structured display and original text when supported.
  • Search uses the available preview. Large files may load only an excerpt; check status and excerpt navigation.

Documents, images and spreadsheets

Supported PDF, DOCX and XLSX files have integrated rendering. Select the required workbook sheet rather than assuming the first one contains all data. Preview does not run Office macros. Image zoom changes display magnification, not stored image dimensions. Expand file details below preview to inspect metadata supported by the format.

Dedicated guides: CSV and separators, image conversion and resizing, audio conversion, names and metadata.

The Preview context command and F3 always open the internal preview in the opposite panel, including XLS and other supported documents. Enter and double-click continue to use normal associated opening.

Internal editor and external applications.

Title: Internal editor and external applications
Summary: F4, syntax highlighting, YAML, JSON formatting and safe saves.
Body:
Current workflow

F2 or Ctrl+N opens a new unnamed text document in the internal editor. Its destination is the panel folder captured when it was created, even after navigating elsewhere. First Save asks only for a filename and extension in an application dialog. Replacing an existing file requires confirmation. Remote saving follows the connection capabilities. New documents default to UTF-8 without BOM and LF; encoding and LF/CRLF remain selectable in the status area. Existing documents preserve their format. Syntax highlighting can be chosen before saving, including shell and RouterOS scripts. Shift+F6 renames a panel file; F2 no longer renames.

Opening and navigation

Select a local text or source file and press F4. The editor has its own window with document tabs; opening the same file again selects its existing tab. Settings include a switch for internal F4 text editing. Office documents and other non-text formats continue to use their external application.

Text and source code

Features include line numbers, highlighting by extension, indentation guides and JSON/YAML folding. Choose 2, 4 or 8 spaces; Tab inserts spaces. A new line inherits indentation and adds one level after a YAML colon or an opening brace/bracket. Check YAML nesting manually; the editor does not automatically rewrite the entire YAML document.

Ctrl+F opens search, Ctrl+H opens replacement of the next occurrence, and Ctrl+G goes to a line. Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y undo and redo edits. Showing spaces and tabs only changes their appearance.

Formatting and validation

JSON formatting preserves exact numeric spellings and key order, including large integers. Invalid JSON and duplicate keys stop formatting rather than being guessed or silently repaired. YAML validation streams parser events without expanding aliases. Validation checks syntax, not application-specific schema or semantics. XML validation prohibits DTD and external entities.

Encoding and saving

Normal saves retain the original encoding, BOM and line endings. UTF-8 and Unicode BOMs are recognized; non-UTF-8 text without a BOM falls back to Windows-1250. Explicit choices include UTF-8, UTF-8 BOM, UTF-16 LE, Windows-1250 and Windows-1252, plus CRLF/LF line endings. Characters unsupported by the selected encoding are not silently discarded.

The complete file is loaded, up to 16 MiB; binary data and links are rejected. Saving checks for changes made by another application and uses a temporary file. A conflict retains your document edits: use Save as, or decide which version to retain before reopening the original. Closing a modified document or the main window offers Save, Discard or Cancel.

Non-text files use the default registered Windows Open action. Executable scripts are sent to a text editor instead of being executed. FTP/SFTP and archive edits continue to use their existing working-copy and upload/commit workflow. See previews, network connections and archives.

F4 and Shift+F4

F4 opens supported text and source code in the internal editor. Excel, Word, PowerPoint, PDF, images, archives and other non-text types go directly to the default Windows Open action, such as Excel or a PDF reader, rather than a separate registered Edit action. Missing or broken associations open the Windows application chooser.

Shift+F4 immediately opens the external application for the current file; menus and the file context menu show this shortcut. Inside the internal editor it opens the current saved document externally. Editing scripts or executables passes them as data to a text editor instead of executing them.

External CSV and HTML editing

Shift+F4 and the external-edit command open CSV directly in Microsoft Excel. If Excel is missing or cannot be located, an error is shown rather than launching an unrelated program. HTML and HTM external editing explicitly uses Windows Notepad instead of a browser. Plain F4 still permits internal CSV and HTML editing. The external-edit toolbar icon has been removed; menus, the context command and Shift+F4 remain.

Choosing an application for an unassociated file

If an extension such as XLS has no default application, F4 and Shift+F4 show the Windows Open with dialog. Choose Excel or another suitable application. If Windows offers a permanent assignment, you can select it yourself; File Compass does not automatically overwrite associations. Broken registered applications use the same chooser. Cancelling simply closes it without an error.

Title: Copying files
Summary: F5, destination folder and transfer progress.
Body:
Current workflow

Setup uses sidebar sections. Progress shows the whole job above a thinner blue current-file bar. Speed and further measurements are under Transfer details. Background docks the job in the bottom activity area; Detail restores it. Read/move errors offer Retry, Skip, Skip all and Cancel. Skipped move sources are retained. A symbolic link or junction is not necessarily a locked file; read the actual reported cause.

Check the original before overwriting. See collisions.

Step-by-step workflow

  1. Open the source in one panel and destination folder in the other. Select files and choose Copy / F5.
  2. Check the item count, destination and filter. The destination normally specifies a folder; use a destination including a new filename only for an appropriate single-file operation.
  3. Choose collision handling and preservation options. Enable SHA-256 verification when you need content checking; this reads additional data and takes more time.
  4. Copy starts the operation; Enqueue schedules it. During transfer, watch the current file, overall progress, speed and any prompts.

Understanding options

Preserve modification time retains the file timestamp; attributes preserve properties supported by the destination filesystem. Copying NTFS permissions requires a suitable filesystem and permissions; ordinary cloud storage does not implement identical semantics. Skipping hidden and system files can intentionally reduce the copied set. Copying empty folders preserves directory structures without files.

Interruption and errors

Cancel retains files already completed; it does not undo the entire batch. Resume only with the matching source and destination. History cannot reconstruct the original content of an overwritten file. See collisions, presets, safe undo and locked files.

Transfer-rate units

Rates use MiB/s: 1 MiB = 1,048,576 bytes. Decimal MB/s use 1,000,000 bytes and would display 4.8576% higher at the same throughput. The transfer rate includes read/write and inline SHA-256 processing; final flushing and optional verification also affect total elapsed time. Isolated screenshots cannot replace a complete-operation comparison under equal conditions.

Title: When a destination file already exists
Summary: Overwriting, skipping and applying a choice to more files.
Body:
Current workflow

Existing and incoming files are shown side by side. Overwrite, Skip and stopping the job remain directly accessible; rename, append and bulk rules use sidebar sections. Equal sizes and timestamps do not prove equal contents. A bulk collision policy lasts only for the current job.

Use content, not just names

A collision means the destination name already exists. Compare sizes, timestamps and, when appropriate, contents. A newer timestamp does not guarantee a better version: device clocks can differ and applications can preserve earlier timestamps.

  • Overwrite replaces destination content; back up the earlier version first if it matters.
  • Skip preserves the destination and continues with other items.
  • Renaming the output preserves both versions when the dialog offers that option.
  • Apply-to-all choices affect later collisions; use them only after confirming they suit the entire batch.

When uncertain, stop and use comparison or checksums. History is not a backup of overwritten content. Space or permission failures are not resolved by choosing a different collision policy.

Title: Creating and extracting archives
Summary: Compression, destination folder, passwords and multipart archives.
Body:
Current workflow

Destination, format and compression level are basic settings; additional options use sidebar sections. File preparation does not show misleading percentage bars; those appear during measurable processing. The selected level is mapped to the relevant archiver. Higher levels do not guarantee smaller output, especially for video, JPEG or already compressed data; uncompressed formats do not use a compression level. An unreadable or locked input offers retry, skip or stop instead of silently omitting it.

Create an archive

  1. Select source files and folders and choose Compress.
  2. Choose archive location, format and compression level. Select a format supported by the recipient, not merely a preferred extension.
  3. Avoid selecting an output archive as part of its own input tree. Read the offered action when the destination already exists.
  4. Create the archive and test that its contents can be read before deleting originals.

Browse and extract

An archive interior is a virtual location. Extract a file safely before using it with an ordinary application. Choose a destination and collision policy. Extracted contents may require much more space than the compressed archive; check destination capacity. A required password does not grant permission to overwrite unrelated files.

Read and write support differ by format. An external archiver may need configuration. For errors check format, damage, password, free space and tool availability. Cancellation does not certify a complete archive. See the archive reference and existing destinations.

Title: Network, NAS and remote connections
Summary: SMB, FTP, FTPS, SFTP and NFS.
Body:
Choose the connection type

Network discovery helps locate devices but is not a complete service inventory. A computer may accept file transfers without announcing itself. Connect directly by known host name or address when discovery does not find it.

  • Windows and NAS shared folders: SMB, for example \\nas-demo\Shared.
  • SSH servers: SFTP, with host-key and user verification.
  • Other protocols must match the service and port actually enabled; the same IP does not imply the same login method.
  • Internet storage uses cloud connections rather than LAN computer discovery.

Saved connection and transfer

  1. Select protocol, address, port and authentication method.
  2. Connect and open a specific folder. Being able to list files does not establish write permission.
  3. Open the local source in the other panel and transfer a small test file first.
  4. After disconnection restore service availability before changing overwrite settings.

VPN transfers also depend on routing and DNS. Testing an IP address and a hostname are different checks. Missing discovery entries may reflect network segmentation or disabled announcements. See the connection reference.

Slow SMB reads

Folder creation and enumeration run outside the UI thread. A read that fails to respond within 15 seconds reports an error and permits refresh; a late older result cannot replace a newer listing. After a folder-creation timeout, refresh and check whether creation eventually succeeded before retrying. Pending system calls cannot always be cancelled immediately. Network entries use file-type icons so reading an individual remote file does not block the shared icon cache.

Title: Opening an SMB share
Summary: Direct UNC paths to a NAS or another computer.
Body:
Open a NAS or computer directly

Enter a UNC path such as \\nas-demo\Shared. The first part is the device name or IP, the second the actual share name, which may differ from its server-local disk or folder name. Direct access can work even when discovery does not list the device.

  1. Check device reachability on the LAN or VPN.
  2. Use an account and domain accepted by that server. A Windows account on another computer does not automatically have share access.
  3. After listing contents, test a small copy if write access is expected.
  4. For regular use save the path as a favorite or use supported network-drive mapping.

Windows may retain a connection to the same device under another account. Changing a password in one dialog does not necessarily end that system connection. Distinguish DNS failures, missing shares, authentication failures and subfolder permissions. See network connections.

Title: Connecting cloud storage
Summary: Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and authorization.
Body:
Add and authorize an account

  1. Open cloud connection management, choose the service and assign a distinguishable connection name.
  2. Complete provider-specific authentication. Google Drive and OneDrive may require consent in a sign-in window.
  3. Confirm the intended account. Two accounts with the same provider are separate connections.
  4. Select the connection in a panel and wait for loading. When switching, check the active connection name and completion.

Google Drive, OneDrive and iCloud

Google may report application-verification or account restrictions; one successful account login does not prove universal public approval. OneDrive access varies with personal or organization account permissions. iCloud may require an additional Apple verification step and renewed authorization after session expiry. Supply only fields requested by the current provider dialog; field meanings are not universal across services.

Transfers and errors

Start with a small test file. Listings can lag and services can limit rate or requests. Renew invalid authorization instead of repeatedly overwriting files. Cloud quota exhaustion is not fixed by changing a local upload folder. Checksums and metadata may differ from local NTFS semantics. See the cloud reference.

Title: Finding files and duplicates
Summary: Name and content searches and duplicate files.
Body:
From names to contents

  1. Choose a root and whether to include subfolders. Wider scopes read more data.
  2. Enter a name mask such as *.jpg, then optional size or date limits.
  3. For content search enter text. PDF and DOCX search reads document text, not OCR from pictures.
  4. Run the search, inspect full paths and open the location or preview.

PDF/DOCX content search supports documents up to 64 MB with a 15-second processing limit. A scan without a text layer may not match visible words. A processing failure or limit is different from genuinely empty content.

Duplicates

Choose folders and wait for size comparison followed by full-content SHA-256. Duplicate files need not share names; equal names do not prove equal contents. Retain at least one copy in every group. Before deleting, check whether separate projects deliberately need their copies. Searching itself deletes nothing. See checksums and other tools.

Title: Comparing and synchronizing folders
Summary: Folder differences and transfer direction.
Body:
Compare first, modify second

Open matching roots and start folder comparison or synchronization. Build the plan before applying it. Verify transfer directions and proposed deletions row by row: synchronization does not automatically mean preserving every file in both directions.

  1. Select roots, recursion and filters.
  2. Wait for comparison to finish; intermediate lists may be incomplete.
  3. Check left/right states, proposed directions and conflicts. Timestamp and size alone do not prove identical content.
  4. Remove unwanted steps or select a suitable conflict policy before confirming execution.
  5. Compare again afterward; another application can invalidate an earlier plan.

Keep backups before synchronization involving deletion. For browsing without changes, use linked panels. For content equality use checksums.

Title: Disk space analysis
Summary: Folder sizes, filters, exports and saved analyses.
Body:
Current workflow

Opening the analyzer does not start a scan. Set Scope and filters, such as minimum size, then choose Start. Results reserve most space for files and the chart. Select the chart type above the chart; other parameters and diagnostics have separate sections. Background docks the window as a bottom activity tile with progress; Detail restores it. Overlapping roots are not counted twice.

Locate space usage

  1. Select a folder or disk and open disk space analysis.
  2. Wait for scanning. Intermediate totals are not final; inaccessible folders can limit results.
  3. Select a list or chart entry and drill into a folder. Size values use aligned columns rather than spacing guesses.
  4. Review largest files, types and ages using available filters. Open the actual location before deciding to delete.

File-size totals can differ from volume usage because of allocation, filesystem metadata, links, compression and permissions. An incomplete or empty result after access failures does not prove unused space. Charts represent size, not file importance.

Export a report when sharing findings and check whether it contains private names or paths. For device health see SMART; for identical copies see duplicates.

Treemap, size shares and multiple folders

By-folder maps show child folders and directly contained files. Up to 512 folders and 1024 direct files are displayed individually; remaining items are included in Other blocks. Selecting Other lists precisely those remaining items. Other grouping modes map the selected chart categories. Large expanded trees create primarily visible row containers and recycle them while scrolling.

Context actions and empty folders

Right-click the tree, map, legend or results for Open in panel, file preview, Copy path and Move to Recycle Bin when applicable. Aggregate blocks cannot accidentally delete a physical parent folder. Scan roots and drive roots are protected from this delete command.

Empty folders lists only genuinely empty, successfully read directories. Filtering files out does not make a nonempty directory eligible. Select multiple rows manually and use their context menu to move them to the Recycle Bin. Each folder is checked again before deletion. Network locations may not support recycling; Windows handles such failures.

Slow USB or network scans

The idle threshold sets how many seconds without progress trigger a warning; 0 disables the warning. This is not automatic termination. Stop requests cancellation and retains partial results. Retry scan first cancels existing work and restarts after it ends. A system read blocked inside a driver or network call must return before cancellation can finish; the application does not forcibly interrupt it. The last path and error help locate the problem.

Title: Language and appearance
Summary: Language changes without restart and theme settings.
Body:
Current workflow

The application uses the unified Balanced design; the original visual design is no longer selectable. Light, dark and system color modes remain available. Updates shows application and component status. A daily check does not download anything by itself. See the Updates topic for details.

Configuration and live language switching

After successful saving the language changes in supported open windows without restarting. Real filenames and user-entered content are never translated. Built-in articles are available in Czech and English; other interface languages explicitly identify English as the article language.

Readability and performance

Interface and file-list fonts are separate settings. With larger fonts, check column and action visibility. Showing hidden/system files changes visibility, not stored attributes. Automatic refresh keeps panels current, but watching a slow UNC location can load the network; manual Ctrl+R is an alternative. Automatic folder views adapt columns to contents; saved custom views have their own rules.

For save failures check access to the configuration folder. Restarting repeatedly cannot fix inaccessible configuration. See command search for custom shortcuts.

Title: Keyboard shortcuts
Summary: F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8 and Ctrl+Q.
Body:
Current workflow

F2 / Ctrl+N: new text file. Shift+F6: rename. Ctrl+T / Ctrl+W: open / close a panel tab. F1: context help. Esc: close a secondary window through its normal safe close path; unsaved changes and running work may require confirmation. An open menu or list consumes the first Escape. Escape does not exit the main application.

Keys and context

Commands depend on the active panel and dialog. Enter opens the current list item but may execute the primary action in a confirmation dialog; read that action before pressing it. Esc normally closes a dialog or cancels its active operation. Keys in text fields may edit text instead of acting on files.

  • Tab switches panels when focus is not inside a dialog.
  • F1 opens context help for the current window.
  • F3 / F4 open viewer / editor.
  • F5 / F6 copy / move; F7 creates a folder, F8 deletes.
  • Ctrl+Q toggles quick preview; Ctrl+R refreshes contents manually.

Custom assignments can change command shortcuts. Check menu captions or custom shortcuts rather than assuming another file manager’s conventions.

Title: Troubleshooting
Summary: Missing network devices, denied access and interrupted transfers.
Body:
Troubleshooting sequence

  1. Record version, build and date from About. Distinguish a single-file failure from a whole-batch failure.
  2. Try a small demonstration file in a new local folder. Local success helps separate format problems from connection or permission failures.
  3. Check destination, free space, permissions, connectivity and other applications holding the file.
  4. For format failures inspect actual content, not just extension. For broken accents change preview encoding.
  5. For media failures reduce parallelism and try a common supported profile. Read the per-file queue error.

Useful bug reports

Describe steps, expected and actual results, location type and exact error. Remove private names, account addresses and credentials from screenshots; reproduce with a nonpersonal sample. Never send tokens, passwords or private keys. About can copy build diagnostics.

Specific guides: locks, CSV, authorization, audio and saving settings.

Title: Moving, renaming and creating folders
Summary: F6, Shift+F6 and F7.
Body:
Moving versus copying

Moving changes the original location; copying retains the source. Open source and destination, select items and use F6 / Move. Verify target path and item count. Moving across volumes or servers may require copying followed by source removal, so it is not necessarily as immediate as renaming within one folder.

Use F7 for a new folder and check which panel is active. Names must be valid on the target system and must not collide with existing items. After partial failures inspect each item; the whole batch is not necessarily rolled back. See batch rename and transaction history.

Title: Deleting files and folders
Summary: F8, confirmation and permissions.
Body:
Review before confirming

Select items and choose Delete / F8. Check count, location and deletion mode in confirmation. Removing a folder includes its contents. Recycle Bin behavior is not available everywhere: network, cloud and some volumes differ from ordinary local storage.

Use lock inspection for in-use files and check the account and attributes for permission failures. Do not dismiss confirmation because names look familiar. Cancelling a batch does not recover files already deleted. History also lists irreversible operations; an entry does not guarantee recovery. Back up needed files beforehand.

Title: Properties, attributes and timestamps
Summary: Alt+Enter and changing attributes.
Body:
Properties are not file content

Properties display or modify supported attributes and timestamps. Read-only may prevent writing; hidden/system attributes affect visibility according to panel settings. Such files are not automatically expendable.

  1. Select a file or intended group and open properties.
  2. Check the scope; a batch setting can affect many files.
  3. Distinguish creation, modification and access times. They are not automatically photo capture dates.
  4. Confirm, then check permissions and destination support if changes fail.

Changing a filesystem date does not necessarily alter EXIF or music tags. Use metadata tools for those. Clouds and other filesystems may support only some properties.

Title: Batch rename
Summary: Rules, numbering and name conflicts.
Body:
Safe workflow

  1. Select inputs and open batch rename. Verify ordering when using a counter.
  2. Build filename and extension patterns. Insert supported tokens from the menu; literal text remains in the output.
  3. Compare old and new names for every row. Check duplicates, empty results and characters invalid on the destination.
  4. Refresh preview after changing a pattern or files, then confirm.

Extensions influence application associations, but renaming is not format conversion. Renaming photo.png to photo.jpg does not create JPEG data; use image conversion. Filesystem creation and photo capture dates differ. See metadata for patterns and reverse writing, and history for limitations after subsequent changes.

Stable preview and recent values

Typing retains the last preview and updates existing row values instead of clearing the list. Start remains disabled until the new calculation succeeds, preventing stale previews from being applied. Arrow buttons beside the name, Find and Replace fields offer ten recent values for each field independently. History is saved when starting an operation and when closing the window, removes duplicates, and survives application restarts.

In the name field, press Alt alone or Alt+Down to open the placeholder menu. Clicking only positions the caret. The chosen token is inserted at the caret or replaces selected text. The same keyboard access applies to fields offering metadata tokens.

Title: Disk health / SMART
Summary: Health, temperature, wear and diagnostic export.
Body:
Current workflow

Physical-drive cards distinguish HDD, SSD and NVMe when the type is available. USB bridges or unknown devices may not expose type or health; a missing value does not mean zero wear. Background docks the tool in the activity area and Detail restores it. A health status cannot guarantee that a drive will not fail.

Select the correct device

Each tile represents a physical disk with available information. Select it and check model, capacity and volume identifiers; several drive letters can belong to one disk. Temperature and summary health are quick indicators, not a complete diagnosis.

  1. Select a disk and wait for refresh.
  2. Review device information and SMART attributes. Raw-value meaning and units depend on manufacturer and device type.
  3. Compare trends over time. One value without context may not establish a failure.
  4. Copy data places text on the clipboard. Export saves an offered format, such as PNG or PDF, according to the dialog.

USB adapters, controllers, remote locations and permissions may limit SMART access. Missing data does not mean healthy or zero errors. Good status cannot guarantee against failure and is not a backup. For occupied file space use the separate disk space analyzer.

Title: Checksums
Summary: Creating and verifying file checksums.
Body:
Verify file contents

A checksum is calculated from all bytes read. Use the matching algorithm, such as SHA-256, to verify a copy or published file. Different algorithms produce different digests and cannot be compared to each other.

  1. Select files and start a supported algorithm.
  2. Wait for reading to finish; large files are limited by storage speed.
  3. Compare the complete digest with a trusted reference for the exact file version.
  4. When saving a list, use correct relative paths for future verification.

A matching checksum from the same untrusted source does not prove software origin or a digital signature. A read failure is not a valid completed digest. Copy verification can also be enabled directly in the operation dialog.

Title: Favorites and workspaces
Summary: Frequently used paths and panel layouts.
Body:
Favorites store frequently used paths; workspaces store related panel layouts and locations. They are not file backups or automatic service authorization.

  1. Open the required directories and arrange panels or tabs.
  2. Save a location or workspace with a clear name, such as Working project.
  3. When restoring it, check disks, VPN and connections. A reused drive letter can point to another device.
  4. Edit or remove obsolete saved locations; that does not delete destination files.

Use linked browsing to follow matching subfolders. Review personal paths and connection names before sharing configuration.

Title: Explorer, Command Prompt and PowerShell
Summary: Tools available in the Start menu.
Body:
External tools for the current location

Start groups Open in Explorer, Command Prompt and PowerShell. Activate the intended panel first. A local folder can serve as a working directory; clouds, archives and virtual locations may lack an ordinary process-accessible path.

  • Explorer opens the location in Windows when accessible.
  • Command Prompt opens the system command environment.
  • PowerShell opens the supported environment according to availability and settings.

Opening a shell itself transfers or deletes nothing. Commands entered afterward affect real data and may not belong to the application’s safe history. Check the displayed working directory before using relative paths.

Title: SFTP and server host keys
Summary: First connection and changed SSH keys.
Body:
Server identity differs from user authentication

SSH/SFTP identifies the server through its host key and authenticates you through an account or user key. On first connection compare the fingerprint with a value obtained from the administrator through another trusted route.

  1. Enter host, port, account and supported authentication method.
  2. Verify the host key. Acceptance records trust for later connections.
  3. After login check the remote folder and read/write permissions.
  4. Investigate changed stored keys: server reinstall, another device at the same IP or an unintended peer.

Blindly accepting changed keys defeats identity verification. SFTP access does not automatically grant permission to run arbitrary server commands. See network connections.

Title: Panels, columns and previews
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
Panels, icons and previews

The Start menu contains Open in Explorer, Run Command Prompt and Run PowerShell, using the active local folder. The former External tools submenu and development-only project-folder shortcut are no longer shown.

Network combines Windows discovery, mapped drives, saved network connections and bounded IPv4 file-service probes on attached private networks. It checks SMB (445), FTP (21), SSH/SFTP (22), implicit FTPS (990) and NFS (2049), showing results progressively. SMB opens shared folders; newly found transfer services open their connection settings before connecting. A listening port indicates a possible service, not confirmed credentials or permissions. Large prefixes are bounded to the adapter's /24, with at most 1,024 candidate addresses and a time limit. Devices on other VPN subnets, IPv6-only devices, nonstandard ports or services hidden by a firewall may require a saved/manual connection. Permission-blocked probes produce a warning in the Network status tooltip.

Layout and navigation

The toolbar cycles side-by-side → stacked → single panel and shows the active layout. View → Panel layout also selects it. Ctrl+H switches dual-panel orientation; Ctrl+Shift+H switches single/last dual layout. Single-panel mode retains the active side; the other side keeps its folder, tabs and connection for later.

The toolbar groups navigation/selection separately from preview/edit/thumbnails. Hidden files toggles hidden/system visibility in both panels while retaining name filters. Invert selection and direction arrows follow it; arrows open the source folder in the other panel. Edit uses F4. Thumbnails change the list, not the preview.

Returning from a subfolder selects that subfolder in the parent. Automatic local refresh leaves the list enabled and applies only added/removed/changed rows, preserving unchanged row instances, marks and scroll position. Network watching is separately configurable and can be disabled for slow paths; Ctrl+R refreshes manually.

Single-panel mode has an adjustable folder tree with Windows names/icons: Home/Quick Access, Desktop, profile, registered cloud folders, This PC, Network and other available system roots such as Libraries, Recycle Bin or Linux. This PC includes local/mapped drives; Network lists computers and devices discovered by Windows, with cached and partial results available during discovery. Computers open their shared folders inside File Compass; other devices open through Explorer. Ctrl+R refreshes discovery. Redirected OneDrive paths come from Windows. Branches load asynchronously on expansion and can be retried. The tree tracks navigation and retains selection/expanded branches. Open an actual filesystem folder for file operations. Dual-panel modes hide the tree, even when older tabs/views requested it.

Unified preview

Preview, View → Preview, Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+Shift+Q control one feature. In dual-panel layouts it replaces the opposite panel; in single-panel mode it appears below the list. Changing layout moves the open preview appropriately and retains lower-preview height. Its header collapses/expands it, and the splitter changes height. Closing restores the opposite panel's previous contents. Hidden/collapsed previews do not continue loading files.

Images, text, syntax-highlighted code, Markdown, binary and hex views are available. Auto chooses the suitable view; Text explicitly displays source, with optional highlighting for supported languages. The formatting checkbox enables/disables code highlighting or rendered Markdown. Hex/Binary retain raw byte views. Find and encoding controls are available; text loads in bounded pages with offset navigation for larger files. Stable selection does not reload an unchanged preview after unrelated folder changes; modifying the selected file does refresh it.

Settings can use internal code/Markdown preview for F3. F4 uses the configured editor; unsupported types are not automatically executed through associations by F3. Settings → Save view and workspaces preserve layout, ratios, visible side, tree and preview state. Automatic view persistence follows its existing exit-saving setting; older settings retain compatible dual-panel defaults.

Rendered documents

Auto mode with formatting enabled supports:

  • PDF through WebView2, with pages, zoom and search.
  • DOCX through docx-preview, including text styles, tables and embedded images within library limits.
  • XLSX/XLS/XLSM/XLSB/ODS through SheetJS, with sheet selection and formatted values. Macros/formulas are not executed; charts and full original styling are unsupported.
  • Older DOC/other unsupported document formats through text extraction where available.

The ready state is shown after rendering. ZIP/RAR/7z in Auto show a read-only archive listing, up to 10,000 items with archive limits; manual Text/Binary/Hex modes remain available.

WebView2 Runtime is neither bundled nor automatically installed. When unavailable, rendering fails or the document exceeds 64 MB, a text/source fallback remains with an official Microsoft runtime link. Install separately and reopen the preview.

Workbook limits: 200 sheets, 2,000 rows and 100 columns per sheet. Compressed documents: 10,000 entries and 128 MB declared expanded size. Files are processed locally, read-only, without retaining a source lock after loading. The renderer permits only the selected file and bundled scripts, blocking unrelated network requests, new windows and downloads. Libraries are bundled, not fetched from a CDN. Licenses are in preview. WebView2 profile/cache uses %TEMP%/FileCompass/WebView2/<installation-id>.

HTML source and page preview

HTML/HTM/XHTML/SHTML in Auto provide Web page / Source code choices. Source is syntax highlighted without changing Office/PDF formatting preferences. Explicit Text mode also supports source highlighting.

Rendered HTML is static: scripts, remote requests, forms, navigation and downloads are blocked. Local CSS/images/fonts may load only from the file's directory or descendants, without traversing reparse links; auxiliary files are limited to 8 MB and unrelated file types are not exposed. If WebView2/rendering is unavailable, source code remains.

Archive/FTP/SFTP HTML previews prepare only the selected HTML file, not separate CSS/images. Code/Markdown views remain read-only.

Archive and remote previews

The same preview works inside an open archive and on FTP/FTPS/SFTP, including the cloud SFTP bridge. Archive files extract into a separate TEMP directory. Remote documents/images download a temporary copy; remote text continues to read a bounded prefix. Preparation shows loading before preview/metadata.

Selection changes/closing cancel preparation and remove temporary copies; source archives/files remain unchanged. Prepared copies are limited to 64 MB, with a 150 ms debounce before extraction/download. SCP uses F3. Encrypted entries require an available password; missing/incorrect passwords show a preview error.

File details and metadata columns

The expandable Details section provides type-dependent information and Copy details. In a lower single-panel image preview, expanded details move beside the image. General fields include name/type/size/creation/modification/attributes and tags.

Images include dimensions, megapixels, DPI, color/depth, transparency, frame count and color-profile presence. EXIF can include capture time, camera/lens, aperture/ISO/exposure/focal length, orientation, GPS, software and copyright; ICO/CUR include variants and dimensions.

PDF details include actual page count, version, stored properties, first-page dimensions and a text excerpt. Scanned pages without text need OCR, which this feature does not provide. Word formats expose properties, authors/editors, cached counts, paragraphs/comments, macro presence and excerpts. Excel formats expose sheets/visibility, saved ranges of the first six sheets, properties and shared-text samples; saved ranges need not equal nonempty cells. Presentation formats expose slide counts/properties/text samples. Office/ODF cached counts can be stale; formulas/macros are not run. Audio/video details depend on readable tags and available codecs.

Metadata columns load in the background; sorting by one also reads other supported files. Leaving the folder cancels work. Missing/unreadable values stay blank. Local/ordinary shared folders support these columns; archive/direct remote/aggregate/system listings do not scan them. PDF counts are read directly; Office/ODF counts are stored values.

Automatic and saved folder views

Settings → Appearance → Automatically adapt view to folder content is off by default. On entering another folder it inspects ordinary nonhidden/nonsystem files: a 60% majority of images selects thumbnails/image columns, documents select author/pages/sheets, music artist/album/title/duration, video duration/resolution. Empty/mixed folders retain the base view. Refreshing the same folder does not override a manually selected view. Disabling the feature restores the original panel view.

After adjusting columns, widths, sorting and display mode, right-click the header to save a view for this folder or this folder and descendants. Saved views apply when automatic views are enabled. More specific paths win; explicit saved views take priority over content inference. Remove saved folder view removes the current-path preset. Presets use config/folder-views.xml; the switch uses config/settings.xml.

Icon libraries

Action sets are Actions.Fluent.fvicons (Windows 11 color), Actions.Flat.fvicons and Actions.Outline.fvicons. FileCompass.Icons.dll contains seven app-icon variants with ten sizes from 16 to 256 px. Settings → Icons previews action/app choices immediately; Save persists them, Cancel restores saved choices. Changing the app icon updates application windows, not the embedded EXE icon or existing Windows shortcuts.

Create shortcut with selected icon writes a .lnk referencing the shared library. For the taskbar, unpin the old item and pin the new shortcut; Windows can cache old pinned icons. Keep the library/application at a stable path. Shortcut Properties → Change icon can browse FileCompass.Icons.dll; an EXE's fixed embedded icon cannot be changed this way.

File icons use Windows associations, including effective user registrations and registered icon resources, with recognizable fallbacks when needed. FVICONS are named-PNG data ZIPs, not executable assemblies. Icon DLLs are mapped as resources without executing code. Original app artwork is separate from third-party Fluent action icons; see libraries/licenses/FLUENT-ICONS-LICENSE.txt.

Title: Copying, recovery and operations
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# File operations and synchronization

Copy, move and delete

Use F5 Copy, F6 Move, F7 New folder and F8 Delete. Copy setup separates destination from file masks/options. Enter runs the default operation, Escape cancels. Choose an explicit collision policy rather than silently overwriting files. Optional controls include SHA-256 verification, timestamps, attributes, NTFS permissions, empty directories and hidden/system exclusions.

Local and network work can run in background queues. The active-job and waiting-job panels show actual work. Network details open when transfer starts. Background hides only the transfer window into the main activity area; click that area to reopen it. It does not minimize the entire application. Speed charts retain the measured history against operation completion. Network ETA uses real transferred bytes over active batch time, includes between-file delays, excludes pauses and waits for a measurement warmup. It remains an estimate.

Network queue lists are compact and scroll for additional items. Speed limits offer presets and a manually editable KiB/s value; 0 is unlimited. Local delete settings may default to the Recycle Bin; deletion still requires confirmation. Shift chooses permanent deletion. The Recycle Bin is unavailable on remote storage and inside archives.

Resume an interrupted network batch

Select the original source files/folders and the same destination, then choose Resume in copy setup. Verified owned partial files resume, missing targets transfer, and complete same-size targets are skipped. Different-size targets transfer again through staging. Already complete files are not fully hash-compared in this mode.

Ownership/checkpoints bind the server, account, source/destination paths, source size/time and sampled block hashes. Changed sources or invalid partial data are rejected. New uploads use .FileCompass-upload-…part; supported checkpoints from older versions remain readable.

A .part.fcinfo.xml sidecar describes original name, destination, length, modification time and transfer identifier. It contains no password or full local source path. This is descriptive only: safe resume also requires File Compass's verified local record in data/transfers. A filename or edited sidecar never authorizes adoption of another file. Successful completion removes the sidecar.

The network batch plan and completed-item receipts are saved during work. Interrupted normal network batches remain recoverable after restarting File Compass or Windows. Startup offers recovery; Commands → Operations → Restore saved tasks opens it manually. Sources/connections are revalidated, and only unfinished items continue. Successful plans are removed. Provider/protocol limits still apply: cloud uploads and non-seekable SCP work may restart the current file.

Folder synchronization

Open two folders, then Commands → Synchronize folders. One-way synchronization and explicit mirroring remain available. For bidirectional work select Bidirectional ↔ and Compare; content comparison is enabled by default but can be disabled for size/time comparison.

Review each row: →, ← or Skip. Bidirectional arrows correspond to the left/right panels. An unresolved ≠ conflict blocks execution; file/folder collisions can be skipped. One-sided items are proposed for copying; differing files propose the newer side, while equal timestamps require a decision.

Bidirectional mode does not propagate deletion or maintain a previous-run database. If both copies changed, proposals use current timestamps and remain editable. Both plan endpoints are validated before the first write; stale plans are rejected. FTP/SFTP use the shared transport layer.

Folder size overview

Alt+Shift+Enter or Commands → Analyze subfolder sizes calculates sizes in the background, with size/share bars. Press again to cancel/hide bars; leaving the folder cancels calculation. Local and mounted filesystems are supported. Logical lengths are measured, not allocated clusters or MFT records. Links are not followed. Skipped locations are counted in the status/tooltip and make totals partial.

Quick image processing

Select images and choose File → Quick image processing. Rotate 0/90/180/270 degrees; keep resolution, limit the longest side or scale by percentage. Longest-side limits never enlarge small images.

Outputs are PNG/JPEG/BMP/TIFF, with JPEG quality control. New copies receive an output suffix; originals and existing outputs are not overwritten. Name collisions are rejected before processing. EXIF orientation is applied before manual rotation. Metadata is not copied. JPEG/BMP replace transparency with white. Multiple frames are retained in TIFF; incompatible single-frame conversion is rejected. Cancellation can leave completed copies.

Move into an archive and split volumes

Alt+F5 supports Move into archive and split ZIP/7z volumes, including passwords. Move requires subfolders and a new output name. The archive is tested, extracted content is SHA-256 compared, empty folders are checked where paths are retained, and sources are revalidated before deletion. Files are locked, verified and deleted through the same handle; only empty directories are removed. A source change stops further deletion. Cancellation can leave some already verified sources removed, with their content retained in the archive.

Volume presets are 100 MB / 700 MB / 4 GB or custom sizes, using multiples of 1024. Outputs include data.7z.001/.002 and .parts.json; ZIP uses .zip.001, not .z01. Open the first volume with all parts together to browse, test or extract. In-place updates are not supported. Creation requires temporary space for a complete archive and never overwrites existing outputs.

Split and combine ordinary files

File → Split file creates .001, .002, … and a .parts.json manifest, retaining the source. File → Combine files finds the series from .001; with a manifest it verifies part counts, lengths and SHA-256 hashes, including the final result. Missing/damaged parts prevent publication.

Other programs' parts can be combined without a manifest, but original hashes and a missing final part cannot be verified. Retain the manifest for your own transfers. Input parts are never deleted; the result requires a new name.

Title: Search, metadata and tools
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# Search, metadata and workflow tools

Search and batch rename

Commands → Find files, the magnifier or Alt+F7 supports semicolon-separated masks, regular expressions, selected items, recursion depth and size ranges. Double-click a result to open its location. Name/size search supports local/SMB/NFS, open archives and FTP/SFTP/SCP through an independent connection. Content search supports local/SMB/NFS files up to 64 MB, using BOM or UTF-8. Results are capped at 20,000.

File/Commands → Batch rename, the A/B icon or Ctrl+M supports local/SMB/NFS files/folders. Archives and direct remote panels support individual rename instead. Masks include [N] name, [E] extension, [C] counter, [N1-3] name substring, [E1] extension character, [RMD] modification date and [hms] time. Find/replace supports regex and case sensitivity. Numeric fields include increment/decrement arrows.

Live previews identify invalid names/collisions and block execution. Temporary names permit swaps. Errors/cancellation roll back in-progress changes; the latest successful batch can be undone.

EXIF/music masks can be combined with counters:

| Mask | Value |

| --- | --- |

| [EXIF.Date] | Capture date, yyyy-MM-dd |

| [EXIF.Time] | Capture time, HH-mm-ss |

| [EXIF.Camera] | Camera make/model |

| [MP3.Artist] | Artist |

| [MP3.Album] | Album |

| [MP3.Title] | Track title |

| [MP3.Track] | Track number, at least two digits |

| [MP3.Year] | Year |

Presets prepare photo/music naming schemes. Missing/unreadable metadata retains the original name and explains why; invalid Windows filename characters become underscores. Reading never changes file contents/tags.

Space marks a folder and calculates recursive size in the background, including archives and supported remote panels. Links are not followed. An error leaves <DIR> and reports the problem rather than presenting an incomplete total.

Metadata search

Alt+F7 → Metadata combines conditions with the General tab's location, masks and depth. Fields include width/height/megapixels, document pages, spreadsheet sheets, presentation slides, author/title/camera, artist/album/media duration/audio bitrate and capture date.

Numeric comparisons support greater/at least/equal/less/at most; text supports contains/equal/starts with. Case sensitivity is shared with normal search. Durations accept hh:mm:ss or d.hh:mm:ss; capture dates compare calendar dates. All conditions must match; missing values do not match.

Examples cover wide photos, PDFs over 20 pages, author names and videos over one hour. Presets change relevant masks/conditions while retaining other restrictions. Conditions persist in search profiles. Results show matched values and can be sent to a panel; the status shows the file being examined and Cancel stops work.

Metadata search supports local folders and ordinary network shares, not archive/direct FTP/SFTP search. Unsupported conditions are not silently ignored. Isolated workers impose time limits and skip unsupported extensions. Availability depends on formats/codecs and file protection/damage. PDF page counts are read directly; Office/ODF may report cached counts.

Duplicates and comparison

Commands → Find duplicates accepts semicolon-separated folders and scans subfolders. Files are grouped by size then compared using full SHA-256. Aliases/hard links to the same physical file count once; symbolic/reparse links are skipped and inaccessible items reported.

Results show groups, names, paths, sizes and a shared preview. Long path prefixes are shortened with full-path tooltips. Mark copies retains the first path in each group and marks the others; adjust manually. Recycle requires confirmation and rechecks content, size, timestamps and physical identity. Each group must retain an unmarked verified representative; changes invalidate the plan. Partial completion remains visible. Download/extract direct remote/archive content first; mounted folders are supported.

Commands → Compare by content / Ctrl+Shift+D accepts two selected files, one in each panel, or manually chosen paths. Text uses colored side-by-side line comparison with difference navigation and case/trailing-space options; binary mode compares bytes. Images use side-by-side or a slider overlay with shared scale/origin. Images decode to at most 4096 px on the long side; limits are 128 MB and 100 million source pixels. Sources remain unchanged; visual comparison does not replace byte comparison. Two duplicate results can use the same dialog through Ctrl-selection and Compare.

Code, Markdown and tags

Preview/Ctrl+Q/Ctrl+Shift+Q show source highlighting or rendered Markdown; the formatting checkbox switches to plain text. Highlighting works in Auto and explicit Text mode. Viewer settings can enable this internal preview for F3; F4 keeps the configured editor.

Markdown supports headings, lists, tables and code blocks. Embedded HTML is not executed, links are inactive and remote images are not downloaded. Text preview reads a bounded initial 128 KiB page.

File → Edit tags (also in the context menu) adds/replaces/removes tags. A quick filter such as #Important selects matching items; Commands → Files by tags also finds tagged files elsewhere. Tags live in the local profile and do not modify file content. File Compass moves/renames preserve tags; external moves are not automatically tracked. Where physical identity is available, a new file at the old path does not inherit old tags.

Workspaces, basket and recursive listings

Workspaces save named sets of tabs, sorting, views, split ratios and filters. They contain no passwords and do not reopen network connections without a user action.

The selection basket collects references from different folders. Delete/F8 removes basket references only; copy/rename/archive act on the referenced files. Recursive contents displays subfolder files with their locations; return using the parent item or Back to normal folder contents. Directory links are skipped; the limit is 100,000 items and inaccessible folders can stop loading with an error. Cancel via Escape/View. Basket/aggregate listings cannot be destination folders: open an ordinary directory first.

Everything and performance

Commands → Fast search with Everything uses a separately installed/running Everything index; only its SDK is bundled. Queries accept Everything syntax and return at most 20,000 results. The helper has a 15-second timeout. Ordinary Alt+F7 search remains available when Everything is unavailable.

Startup can use a JIT profile on later runs. Thumbnails load for realized rows and release images outside the visible area. Same-folder refresh applies incremental row changes and preserves selection/scroll. Performance depends on storage, antivirus and available caches.

Title: Archives and archivers
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# Archives and optional archivers

File Compass browses archives as folders and uses the bundled 7-Zip engine for supported formats. ZIP, 7z, TAR/GZ and supported external RAR/ARJ/LHA creation are available according to the selected format/tool. Existing ARJ/LHA/TAR archives have read-only limitations. Archive operations enforce path, entry-count, memory, elapsed-time, expanded-size, free-space and nesting limits configurable in Settings → Archives. Passwords remain outside worker command-line arguments.

Compression progress shows the current file, operation completion and compression-ratio history. The chart's horizontal axis is operation completion (0–100%); the vertical axis is output/input percentage and can exceed 100%. The connected samples show how the ratio changes during the operation. See operations for verified move-to-archive and split ZIP/7z volumes.

Obtain optional tools

Settings → Archives can find an existing installation, select an EXE, or open Get add-on / Get WinRAR/RAR. Download begins only in the separate download window. Existing configured/common/PATH installations are used without downloading.

ARJ32 and LHa are prepared under plugins/archivers beside the program, without modifying Windows or Program Files. The window is modeless and supports cancellation. Completion saves the path; manually configured paths remain supported.

WinRAR uses RARLAB's original installer. After downloading, choose Run installer and complete its normal installation steps. File Compass does not run it automatically, install silently or redistribute a standalone Rar.exe. It subsequently searches for the installation; use Find WinRAR if installation is still running.

Sources and licenses

  • WinRAR/RAR 7.23 x64: https://www.rarlab.com/download.htm ; EULA https://www.rarlab.com/license.htm . Trial software, up to 40 days without buying a license. Downloading does not include a license.
  • ARJ32 3.31: https://arj32.com/ . Shareware under ARJ Software's supplied terms. The original ZIP/nested SFX are extracted only; SFX installation/test commands are not executed. Original license/documentation files are retained.
  • LHa 1.14i, GnuWin32: https://gnuwin32.sourceforge.net/packages/lha.htm . The original distribution and documentation are retained. This is the LHa compressor, not the Lhasa extractor.

RAR/ARJ/LHA creation runs external processes without passwords in arguments. Legacy ARJ/LHA filename-encoding limitations still apply.

Integrity and maintenance

Downloads use certificate-validated HTTPS, a 128 MiB maximum and time limits. Pinned versions, URLs and SHA-256 package/EXE hashes are in ArchivePluginInstaller.cs. ARJ is verified before its nested SFX is opened; WinRAR installers also require Authenticode verification before publication and execution. Changed upstream content is rejected.

ARJ/LHA extraction uses the bundled verified codec in an isolated worker with normal archive/path limits. Prepared directories are published atomically; cancelled/failed downloads do not activate a tool. Managed archivers are verified and held open before execution. User-managed installations outside the add-on store use the chosen path.

There is no automatic search for the latest EXE or automatic update. A new managed release requires updated pinned metadata, license/package review and integration tests. A newer personal installation can be selected manually.

Title: Cloud accounts, authorization and transfers
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
Account, service and local connection

A connection has a local display name, provider and authorization for a particular account. Two Google accounts are separate connections. Tabs can retain location identity without automatically repeating login at startup.

Google Drive and OneDrive

New Google sign-ins use the publisher configuration when supplied with the installation; ordinary users then do not enter their own Client ID or Client Secret. Missing publisher configuration or consent is not a folder password problem. Each user separately grants access. Current application-verification status is determined by Google, not established or guaranteed by this help article.

OneDrive can require a drive or library choice. Work or school accounts may require administrator consent. A provider may display an integration tool name during sign-in; verify the account and permissions on the actual service page.

iCloud and verification questions

iCloud uses the Apple authentication and verification flow supported by the current integration. Additional codes or confirmations are provider-specific. Follow the displayed question instead of assuming every provider uses the same ID/password fields. Renew expired authorization by signing in again. Apple account policy and service availability can affect access.

Transfers and temporary previews

Cloud panels use the shared network queue for supported file operations. Browsing can continue where available. Interrupted uploads may restart the current file; handle completed targets according to the chosen collision policy. Native provider documents can be exported only where supported. Preview and editing may prepare a temporary local copy within processing limits.

Renew, disconnect and revoke

Profiles copied from another computer or Windows user may need new authorization. Local credential protection is not transferred by copying program files. Before removing an account finish or cancel transfers and disconnect its panels. Disconnect retains saved authorization; Remove account deletes local configuration, not cloud files. Revoke consent separately in provider account settings when access must end there as well.

Never include passwords, tokens or private keys in screenshots or reports. The local cloud helper is not intended to be exposed to the LAN. This connection method does not mount cloud storage as an Explorer drive letter. See adding accounts, network transfers and troubleshooting.

Title: Third-party notices
Summary: Complete reference guide.
Body:
﻿# Third-party notices

Paths below refer to the installation root unless a source path is stated. Original upstream license/copyright texts are retained with each component; this English inventory does not replace them.

libcurl 8.22.0 and libssh2 1.11.1

Network operations use the native FileCompassNetwork.dll adapter in plugins/network. It statically links libcurl (curl/MIT-like license), libssh2 (BSD-3-Clause) and dependencies from the official curl 8.22.0_3 Windows x64 package. libcurl handles FTP/FTPS; libssh2 handles SFTP/SCP/SSH. LibreSSL 4.3.3 supplies cryptography. Dependencies include zlib-ng, zstd, Brotli, libpsl, the public suffix list, nghttp2, nghttp3 and ngtcp2.

Original notices are in plugins/network/licenses; BUILD-MANIFEST.txt lists exact components/source links and the plugin manifest records package provenance/hashes. Static libraries/headers/original downloads are build-time inputs under source/downloads/network; adapter sources/build scripts are in source/native. No separate runtime installation is required. FluentFTP, SSH.NET and WinSCP are no longer runtime components.

Sources: https://curl.se/windows/ and https://libssh2.org/.

External SSHFS support

WinFsp — Windows File System Proxy, Copyright (C) Bill Zissimopoulos: https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp (GPLv3 with FLOSS exception; commercial licensing https://winfsp.dev/com/).

SSHFS-Win: https://github.com/winfsp/sshfs-win ; component licenses/sources are listed in its License.txt/repository.

WPF UI / WPF UI Abstractions (lepo.co), MIT. The .NET Framework 4.7.2 libraries run under File Compass's .NET Framework 4.8 target. Microsoft dependencies: System.Memory 4.6.3, System.Buffers 4.6.1, System.Numerics.Vectors 4.6.1 and System.Runtime.CompilerServices.Unsafe 6.1.2 (MIT).

according to their action. Asset import: tools/fetch-fluent-icons.cjs.

Licenses are in preview. Documents render locally.
